elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates without requiring written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant includes Client's affiliates only “upon written notice to TrueLink,” so affiliate coverage is conditional rather than automatic.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no licence rights for contractors acting on Client's behalf.
No perpetual duration is stated. The clause does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are inapplicable.
No irrevocability protection is stated. The clause does not demonstrate that paid-up licences are inapplicable.

elements.element: Any subscription licence is terminable only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not limit termination of a subscription licence to an uncured material breach, and it does not demonstrate that subscription licences are inapplicable.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors without limitation to a particular type of succession transaction.
elements.evidence: Transfer without approval is permitted only to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets, not to successors generally.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 15 removes the approval requirement for assignment “to a successor by merger or sale of substantially all assets,” which covers customary M&A succession.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the fallback but not the preferred position. It is not minimal because the successor-assignment exception is made available to either party, unnecessarily expanding TrueLink's assignment rights when the requested licence protection concerns Client. The edits otherwise leave the existing commercial terms operative and introduce no direct contradiction.
